messages:
oncall-bot: Pager: P1 - high queue depth observed in batcher-rt (us-west-2), multiple client timeouts reported :rotating_light:

sara: Ack. I'm seeing the spike in the batcher queue too — requests are queuing for >300ms before dispatch, and some clients are timing out. Investigating root cause of continuous batching behavior.

michael: GPU pool `gpu-pool-3` CPU/GPU load jump at 2024-06-18T19:17:12Z, throughput per instance dropped ~30%. Looks like very long sequences are forcing larger batches and increased KV pressure.

jia: Quick mitigation idea: throttle batching aggressiveness. If we reduce max_batch_size and increase batch_delay_ms we can favor smaller batches (higher latency) but avoid OOM backpressure and excessive queuing. Propose immediate change: max_batch_size 64 -> 8, batch_delay_ms 5 -> 40.

omar: Agree. Also recommend soft tenant rate-limits for top offenders. We can push a per-tenant RPS cap for top 5 tenants and reduce concurrency slots from 16 -> 4 for those tenants.

nyla: Customer impact: SE reports for three customers (acct-132, acct-88, acct-7) with >5% 5xx/timeout. SEs notified. Will prepare one-paragraph incident note for affected customers.

sara: Proposed live runbook (short):
- Step A: Apply batcher config change in us-west-2 (rolling)
- Step B: Push per-tenant soft RPS caps for top 5 tenants
- Step C: Disable streaming for "best-effort" tier (to reduce streaming overhead)
- Step D: Monitor queue length, p95 latency, GPU utilization for 15m.

Anyone object to doing this immediately? We need to trade latency for throughput temporarily.

michael: No objections. I'll apply the batcher change and watch metrics. Command I'll run from ops jumpbox:
```
# roll batcher params (rolling restart, 3m window)
rwctl set batcher --region us-west-2 --set max_batch_size=8 --set batch_delay_ms=40 --rolling 3m
```

omar: I'll patch the tenant rate-limits config now. Using the quick patch below:
```
kubectl -n inference patch configmap tenant-rate-limits -p '\n{"data":{"heavy-tenants":"acct-42:1rps,acct-88:1rps,acct-132:1rps,acct-7:1rps,acct-199:1rps"}}'\n
```

prod-alerts-bot: System: 5xx rate increased to 6.2% (5m window) at 2024-06-18T19:18:34Z — correlating with batcher queue growth.

sara: Pushing disable of streaming for best-effort now (config toggle):
```
# toggle streaming off for best-effort tier
rwctl set routing --tier best-effort --set streaming_enabled=false --region us-west-2
```

michael: Batch config change applied at 2024-06-18T19:20:05Z. Rolling restarts in progress. Watching p95 token latency and queue depth.

logs (sample before -> after):
```
# before
queue_depth: 320 -> p95_token_latency: 420ms -> 5xx_rate: 6.2%
# after (19:22 UTC)
queue_depth: 22 -> p95_token_latency: 680ms -> 5xx_rate: 1.8%
```

nyla: Noted. SEs updated. Customers acknowledged that we'll see slightly higher latency but service continuity prioritized :thumbsup:.

omar: Rate-limit patch applied at 19:21:10Z. Observed immediate drop in per-tenant RPS for top tenants, freed up ~3k tokens/sec.

prod-alerts-bot: System: 5xx rate decreased to 1.7% (5m window) at 2024-06-18T19:24:01Z.

sara: Good. Immediate metrics look positive. We'll keep the batching config and rate-limits in place for now and reassess in 2 hours. If stable, we plan a controlled rollback to more aggressive batching during a low-traffic window.

michael: Handing overnight watch to me at 19:45 UTC. I'll keep an eye on GPU memory pressure and any regression in latency. Runbook link: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/batcher-mitigation

nyla: I'll draft the customer-facing incident note and include mitigation steps + ETA for rollback.

sara: Thanks team. Quick notes for post-incident followup: collect representative traces for long-seq requests, check whether batching heuristics need sequence-length awareness, and add an alert for sustained queue depth > 200.

michael: Acknowledged. Leaving tracing collection running. If anything spikes tonight I'll page back. :rotating_light:
